items.title: ASPIRE Trial: Adding Docetaxel to Hormonal Therapy and Apalutamide for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 clinical trial is testing whether adding the chemotherapy drug docetaxel to the standard combination of hormonal therapy and apalutamide improves outcomes for men with newly metastatic prostate cancer. Docetaxel is a well-established chemotherapy that stops cancer cells from dividing. The trial is currently recruiting patients to compare the two treatment approaches.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Abiraterone Study for First-Line Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial evaluates whether combining olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) with abiraterone works better than abiraterone alone as initial treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is designed for patients who have not yet received chemotherapy or newer hormonal agents at the castration-resistant stage. The trial is no longer enrolling new patients but continues to follow those already enrolled.

items.title: TulmiSTAR-02: Tulmimetostat Combinations for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-phase trial is testing tulmimetostat, a drug that targets cancer through epigenetic mechanisms, in combination with either darolutamide or abiraterone for men with newly metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study aims to determine safe doses and evaluate how well these combinations work. It is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: PREDICT Trial: Genetic Testing to Guide Treatment for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial uses genetic testing of tumor tissue to assign patients to specific treatments based on their cancer's DNA and RNA abnormalities. Treatments include valemetostat (an EZH1/EZH2 inhibitor), carboplatin chemotherapy, or cabazitaxel chemotherapy. The goal is to determine whether matching treatments to genetic changes improves outcomes in metastatic prostate cancer.

items.title: AMO959 Combined with Lutetium PSMA-617 for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-phase study combines AMO959 with lutetium-177 PSMA-617 (Pluvicto) radioligand therapy and an androgen receptor inhibitor for men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have already tried one hormonal agent. The trial is evaluating safety and early evidence of effectiveness. It is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: PSCA-CAR T Cell Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial studies genetically modified immune cells (CAR T cells) that target a protein called PSCA found on prostate cancer cells. The modified T cells are designed to recognize and kill cancer cells. The study is determining the safest dose and evaluating side effects in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, but is no longer enrolling new patients.

items.title: Terbium-161 PSMA Radioligand Therapy Study in Taiwan
items.summary: This phase 1 trial is testing a new radioactive therapy called 161Tb-PSMA-I&T, which uses the element terbium-161 instead of the standard lutetium-177. Terbium-161 may deliver more targeted radiation to cancer cells. The study is evaluating safety, how the drug distributes in the body, and early effectiveness in Taiwanese men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: SX-682 Plus Enzalutamide for Androgen Receptor Inhibitor-Resistant Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests SX-682 combined with enzalutamide in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer whose disease has progressed despite previous treatment with androgen receptor inhibitors. SX-682 targets immune pathways that may help overcome resistance. The trial is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Abiraterone Study for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates luxdegalutamide (an androgen receptor inhibitor) at two different doses combined with abiraterone, compared to standard androgen receptor inhibitors, in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study aims to identify the best dose and assess effectiveness and safety. It is currently recruiting.

items.title: Real-World Study of Olaparib in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This observational study in France is collecting information about how olaparib is used in everyday practice for men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. It examines treatment sequencing, effectiveness, side effects, and patterns of genetic testing for BRCA mutations to help inform future clinical practice. The study is currently recruiting.

items.title: TulmiSTAR-01: Tulmimetostat and Luxdegalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests the combination of tulmimetostat (an epigenetic drug) and luxdegalutamide (an androgen receptor inhibitor) compared to standard care in men with progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is evaluating safety and effectiveness of this novel combination. It is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Nivolumab Plus Radium-223 for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial combines nivolumab (an immunotherapy drug) with radium-223 (a radioactive therapy for bone metastases) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to determine if combining these two treatments is safe and potentially effective. The trial is no longer enrolling new patients.

items.title: DNA Repair Defects Study: Abiraterone, Olaparib, or Combination in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial assigns patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and specific DNA repair gene mutations to receive either abiraterone, olaparib, or both treatments combined. The study focuses on patients with mutations in genes like ATM, BRCA1, and BRCA2 to determine which approach works best for different genetic profiles.

items.title: AZD5305 Combined with Hormonal Agents for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates AZD5305, a PARP inhibitor, when combined with new hormonal agents in patients with metastatic prostate cancer. The study is assessing safety, how the drug works in the body, and early signs of effectiveness. The trial is no longer enrolling new patients.

items.title: A-CAR032 CAR T Cell Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This first-in-human phase 1 trial tests A-CAR032, a CAR T cell therapy, in adults with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after androgen receptor inhibitor treatment. The study evaluates safety, effectiveness, and whether the treatment can be manufactured for patients ineligible for standard treatments. It is currently recruiting.

items.title: Real-World Experience with Lutetium PSMA-617 in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This observational study collects information about how lutetium-177 PSMA-617 (Pluvicto) affects quality of life in everyday clinical practice for men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study tracks patients' experiences during treatment and after disease progression to understand real-world outcomes.

items.title: Lutetium PSMA-617 with Liver-Directed Therapy for Liver Metastases
items.summary: This phase 1b trial combines lutetium-177 PSMA-617 radioligand therapy with liver-directed treatments in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have liver metastases. The study aims to determine if combining these approaches is safe for patients whose cancer has spread to the liver. It is currently recruiting.

items.title: AMG 509 Study for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates AMG 509 alone and combined with abiraterone or enzalutamide in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is assessing safety, how the drug works in the body, and early effectiveness. Currently, only certain expansion cohorts are open to enrollment.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Combinations for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, alone or combined with other treatments for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety, identifies effective doses, and measures PSA levels during treatment. It is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: BPX-601 CAR T Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 study will test BPX-601, a CAR T cell therapy made from the patient's own immune cells, in men with advanced prostate cancer that has returned and spread despite treatment. The study will evaluate side effects, determine the best dose, and assess how well it works against prostate cancer. The trial is preparing to begin recruitment.

items.title: TD001 Antibody-Drug Conjugate for PSMA-Expressing Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates TD001, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting PSMA, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is assessing safety, drug levels in the body, and early signs of anti-tumor activity. It is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: TRC003 Study for Progressive PSMA-Positive Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates TRC003 injection in patients with progressive PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have been treated with androgen receptor inhibitors or chemotherapy. The study is testing three different doses with up to six treatment cycles, recruiting 90 participants to assess safety and effectiveness.

items.title: Real-World Study of Darolutamide Plus Hormone Therapy in Germany
items.summary: This observational study in Germany examines how well darolutamide combined with hormone therapy works for men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer in everyday medical practice. The study collects information about effectiveness and side effects to understand real-world outcomes outside of clinical trials. It is currently recruiting.

items.title: Nuclear Medicine Perspective on PSMA Radioligand Therapy Success and Limitations
items.summary: This medical review discusses lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy from a nuclear medicine perspective, highlighting its success in precisely targeting cancer and providing rapid pain relief. However, it notes that disease recurrence is nearly inevitable despite good initial responses, with modest survival benefits in trials. The review emphasizes the need for interdisciplinary research to improve outcomes.

items.title: PROQURE-I Phase 1: Adding Lutetium PSMA-617 to Standard Treatment for N1 Prostate Cancer
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This phase 1 study added concurrent lutetium-177 PSMA-617 radioligand therapy to standard radiation and hormone therapy in 14 patients with lymph node-positive (N1M0) prostate cancer. No serious toxicity was observed, and the treatment appeared safe. This represents a novel approach to combining radioligand therapy with curative-intent treatment for locally advanced disease.

items.title: Radiopharmaceutical Therapy in Oncology: Advances and FDA Approvals
items.summary: This comprehensive review discusses the transformation of cancer treatment through radiopharmaceutical therapy, which delivers targeted radiation to cancer cells. It highlights FDA approvals of lutetium-177 PSMA-617 (Pluvicto) for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and lutetium-177 DOTA-TATE for neuroendocrine tumors. The review emphasizes the "radiotheranostic" approach that combines imaging and therapy for personalized treatment.

items.title: Bavdegalutamide Plus Abiraterone Phase 1b Trial Results
items.source: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
items.summary: This phase 1b trial tested bavdegalutamide (ARV-110), a PROTAC drug that degrades androgen receptor, combined with abiraterone in 45 men with metastatic prostate cancer progressing on abiraterone. The combination was safe with a median treatment duration of 35.7 weeks. Thirteen patients achieved at least 50% PSA decline, suggesting the combination may help overcome resistance to abiraterone.

items.title: Top Advances in Radiopharmaceutical Therapy for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review highlights significant developments in radiopharmaceutical therapy for prostate cancer in 2025, building on the foundation of radium-223 for bone metastases and expanding with PSMA-targeted imaging and therapy. The field has evolved from pain palliation to cancer-directed treatments with the approval of PSMA-targeted agents, representing a major advance in prostate cancer management.

items.title: Terbium-161 PSMA Therapy After Lutetium-177 PSMA Progression
items.summary: This study evaluated 15 patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who received terbium-161 PSMA-617 radioligand therapy after their disease progressed on lutetium-177 PSMA-617. Terbium-161 emits different types of radiation that may be more effective. The study provides early insights into safety and effectiveness of this alternative radioligand for patients who have exhausted standard options.

items.title: Optimizing Care for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.source: American Society of Clinical Oncology educational book. American Society of Clinical Oncology. Annual Meeting
items.summary: This educational review provides a practical framework for managing metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, integrating new treatments including androgen receptor inhibitors, chemotherapy, PARP inhibitors, and radioisotopes. The review addresses the complexity of treatment sequencing and decision-making, particularly as patients are now receiving more intensive treatments earlier in their disease course.

items.title: Novel Therapies Beyond Androgen Receptor Inhibition for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This comprehensive review discusses new treatment strategies for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer beyond hormonal therapies, including PARP inhibitors for DNA repair defects, PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy, bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, and immune checkpoint inhibitors. The review emphasizes the role of molecular profiling and liquid biopsy in guiding personalized treatment decisions.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Prognostic Factors for PSMA Radioligand Therapy
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes evidence on factors that predict outcomes for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer receiving PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy. The study identifies clinical, blood test, and imaging features that help predict which patients are most likely to benefit from this treatment, providing evidence to guide treatment decisions.
